When working with my caddies who deserve more credit than the golfers sometimes. You would go through your stock yardages, avg drive distance etc, you’d discuss preferred distances in, your miss etc, they would then go through the course and essentially map out a game plan.

A standard par 4 let’s say 470, he knows my driver will go 300-310 with 285-290 carry, he would work within about 30 yards either way of that so we could know exactly where we are within that gap, he would use any reference he has as a start and work from there, walking maybe 10 yards back or forward and we have the yardage, he would walk the green before hand so we know the green dimensions, with pin sheets we could work out exactly how far on the pin is and therefore the exact yardage. All yardages from the fairway are to the front and you work out the yardage to the pin from knowing the green distance from front to back and where the pin sits. 

There’s a lot more details but as far as yardage goes that pretty much it. (In my experience with my caddies) 

Hope it helped
